title: CI scope skips every job on a push that changes only docs/records.md when the head before the push was fully green
why: Owner ruling own-830-c-ci-scope-green-before-head (page item 830, option c, 15:02 CST Nov 14, no note); the owner chose a widening knowingly. Today a ready green PR meets a records-page push at merge (about 4 of 11 PR-merge commits since Nov 13 and 20 of 38 since Nov 10, triage's approximate count from a shallow clone) and a second full CI follows (44 min 32 s in the one run measured, n=1: run 43583006785, #3349 head 3128df369). The change, as the records lane described it (relayed, unread by triage): ci-scope.sh reads the push's before-head, checks that head's run was fully green and the push changed docs/records.md alone, then sets every job flag false; all-jobs-passed counts those skipped jobs as passed. It changes ci-scope.sh, checks.yml and lint/test_ci_scope.py, and edits the script's own fail-safe list, so it needs review round 3 and the net-value test. Unmeasured: the gain (jobs flagged false still start and skip), and a fail-safe against a wrong green read. GRANT SCOPE: only a push whose whole change is docs/records.md after a fully green head; any other change in the push runs CI as today. First act of a lane: read ci-scope.sh line 17 on (it diffs the whole PR against its base, never the push) and the test file, write the red tests first: a records-only push after a green head skips; a records-only push after a red or unknown head runs; a push that touches one other file runs; a hand-edited page does not skip beyond what main's check allows. Triage reads the before-head result as unknown when the run cannot be read, never as green. Kin: records-page-before-ready (the lane that described it), ready-push-merges-main (item 840), review-carries-own-record-commits. LANE 15:11 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 15:09, its pick, told the lane 15:08): the records lane session_013NEJKzSUfg1GuTrqARWDNd builds it on a new branch; it also tells the coordinator whether #3396 is moot. MECHANISM CHANGED 15:14 CST Nov 14 (the records lane, accepted by the coordinator 15:12 as its own undoable pick; triage read none): the lane changed the mechanism from the step text (the push's before-head) to a green-head reader, because the ready route has no push before-head (the draft run skips scope). The delta is measured from the newest earlier fully green head and must be exactly docs/records.md. Round 3 and the net-value test stay. TRIAGE'S FLAG (reading, unchecked): the owner's option c named "when the head before the push was fully green"; a grant covers the act it names, never a variant (rule outcomes-grant-covers-named-act). My reading is that the new form skips the same or fewer pushes: it skips only when the whole delta from a fully green head is records.md, so an intervening push that changed another file blocks the skip, which the before-head form also does when that head was not green. Where the two differ is not proven. The round 3 reviewer reads this case first: if it reads the new form as skipping anything the owner's form would not, the change goes to the owner as a question before it merges. COORDINATOR READS THE FLAG THE SAME WAY 15:16 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 15:15): the owner's literal "head before the push" has no value on the ready route (a draft push, then ready_for_review), so it could never skip there; the green-head form skips there, which is the owner's aim (stop the second full CI after the ready records push). It skips fewer where a code change sits between the green head and the records push (the delta then holds more than docs/records.md). UNPROVEN: a chain of records-only pushes, where an earlier push's run was itself a skip counted as green. Plan kept: the round 3 reviewer reads those cases first; the change goes to the owner as a question before it merges if it skips anything his form would not; the coordinator will not mark it ready before that is settled. LANE QUESTION 16:03 CST Nov 14 (lane records-page-before-ready, 16:02, from draft #3426; triage read no code): the change built under owner ruling own-830-c skips the macOS, checks-windows, pointer, shoot, mutation and sweep work, but checks-windows-guard (3 shards), checks-windows-merge (5), checks-windows-rest (2) and checks-hooks gate their steps on no flag, so they still run on a records-only push (round 1 reviewer read checks.yml lines 1761-2140; the lane did not re-read; gain unmeasured). Lane recommends accepting the partial gain until measured; it builds nothing more on #3426. TRIAGE READING: the owner's ruling says "skip every job" and "sets every job flag false"; the lane's build falls short of the named act, so gating the rest is the owner's own act, not a variant. Not posted to the owner as a new question; it goes to him only if the follow-up widens past the ruling (for example, skips a job his words do not name). The gap is reported to him in the next report.
note: Filed 15:04 CST Nov 14 by triage. Tracker: the coordinator. No lane yet; the lane of records-page-before-ready (session_013NEJKzSUfg1GuTrqARWDNd) may be the one that builds it.
